title: Give your agent a retry limit
description: Recover from a failed lookup and stop safely when the tool remains unavailable.
objective: Recover from a temporary tool failure, then stop without an invented answer when the retry budget is exhausted.

sources.claim: An agent receives environmental feedback and can stop at a maximum iteration count.
The application returns the outcome of a client tool call to the model.

beats.title: A connected tool can still fail
beats.body: Your loop already executes lookups, returns their results, and stops on an answer. Now the inventory sometimes returns an error instead of a count. The program must choose whether to retry or stop. This lesson uses a read-only lookup, so retrying does not place another order or change inventory. That is not true for every tool. The practice model is simulated, and the tool's failures are declared in each case.

beats.title: Inspect an unfinished task
beats.goal: This case fails its first lookup. Run the supplied program and inspect the error. Stopping without invented data is valid error handling, but it does not complete this inventory task.

beats.goal: The first lookup fails, but another attempt can succeed. Change the error handling and retry allowance. Return the error to the conversation and allow one retry, then inspect how the next lookup finishes the task.

beats.title: Recover or report the failure
beats.goal: Build one program that handles all three cases. It must finish when inventory becomes available, and report a tool error when retries cannot recover the lookup. It must not invent stock counts or use the model-call limit as its normal error exit. Run tests your unchanged program against every case.

beats.title: A retry is another attempt, not a guarantee
beats.body: Your loop can recover from one failed read and stop when further attempts exceed its allowance. Recovery produces an answer supported by tool results. A persistent failure produces an error and no answer. Those are different outcomes. The retry allowance limits error recovery, while the model-call limit bounds the whole loop. This lesson's one-retry policy is a practice choice. Real tools need policies that account for their failure modes and whether repeating an action changes external state.

beats.intro: Switch between a temporary failure and an ongoing outage. Compare zero, one, and two retries. Then lower the model-call limit and inspect which limit stops the loop. Free play does not change your challenge result.
